definitionEn: The energy used to run machines, lights, and other equipment.
example: The storm cut the power to thousands of homes across the city.

definitionEn: A form of energy that flows through wires and powers lights, machines, and appliances.
example: Our village received electricity for the first time in the spring of 2015.

definitionEn: The energy that makes something warm or hot.
example: The heat from the furnace kept the whole house warm all winter.

definitionEn: A thick liquid, often burned or refined, used as fuel.
example: Many factories still depend on oil to run their heavy machinery.

definitionEn: A black rock that is burned to produce heat and electricity.
example: The old power station burned coal to produce electricity for the town.

definitionEn: A material that is burned to produce heat or power for engines.
example: Cars that use less fuel save money and produce fewer emissions.

definitionEn: Harmful substances that make air, water, or land dirty and unsafe.
example: Heavy traffic causes air pollution that harms the health of city residents.

definitionEn: Powered by or producing electricity.
example: She bought an electric car to reduce her fuel costs each month.

definitionEn: A glass object that gives out light when electricity passes through it.
example: The old bulb in the hallway flickered and then went out.

definitionEn: A device that turns electricity on or off in a circuit.
example: Please turn off the switch before you change the light bulb.

definitionEn: To put electrical energy into a battery so that it can be used again.
example: Remember to charge your phone before you leave for the airport.

definitionEn: A device at the end of a cable that fits into a socket to supply power.
example: The electrician replaced the broken plug on the kettle's cord.

definitionEn: A wall built across a river to hold back water and create a reservoir.
example: The new dam on the river will supply power to three provinces.

definitionEn: A long tube used to carry water, gas, or oil from one place to another.
example: A leaking gas pipe under the road forced workers to close the street.

definitionEn: A thick wire or bundle of wires that carries electricity or signals.
example: The engineers laid new underground cables to carry power to the island.

definitionEn: A device that gives light, often by electricity, placed on a table or stand.
example: She switched on the lamp beside her bed and kept reading.

definitionEn: Materials that are thrown away because they are no longer useful.
example: The factory reduced its waste by recycling metal and plastic on site.

definitionEn: To process used materials so that they can be made into new products.
example: Families are encouraged to recycle bottles, paper, and cans every week.

definitionEn: Light and warmth that come directly from the sun.
example: The rooftop panels produce plenty of power on days of bright sunshine.

definitionEn: Water falling in drops from clouds in the sky.
example: A week of steady rain filled the reservoir behind the dam.

definitionEn: To send out gas, light, heat, or a sound into the surrounding area.
example: Burning coal emits large amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.

definitionEn: To make air, water, or land dirty or harmful by adding waste.
example: Factories that pollute rivers often face heavy fines from the government.

definitionEn: To produce or create something, such as electricity or heat.
example: The hydroelectric plant generates enough electricity for half the region.

definitionEn: Formed from the remains of ancient plants or animals, as in coal, oil, and gas.
example: Many countries are trying to reduce their dependence on fossil sources of energy.

definitionEn: A large artificial lake that stores water for drinking, farming, or electricity.
example: The reservoir behind the dam stores enough water for the entire province.

definitionEn: The force that pushes electric current through a circuit, measured in volts.
example: The transformer lowers the high voltage before it reaches homes.

definitionEn: A flow of electric charge through a conductor, such as a wire.
example: A strong electric current flowed through the wires and lit the whole street.

definitionEn: A unit of power equal to one thousand watts.
example: The air conditioner uses about two kilowatts of power every hour.

definitionEn: A unit of power equal to one million watts.
example: The new plant can produce several megawatts of electricity during peak hours.

definitionEn: To cover or line something to stop heat, sound, or electricity from passing through.
example: We insulated the attic to keep the house warm and reduce heating bills.

definitionEn: The system of supplying fresh air to a building and removing stale air.
example: Good ventilation in the kitchen removes smoke and keeps the air fresh.

definitionEn: A device that automatically controls the temperature of a room or system.
example: Setting the thermostat two degrees lower can save a surprising amount of energy.

definitionEn: A machine or device for household use, such as a fridge or washing machine.
example: Old appliances often waste electricity, so replacing them can lower bills.

definitionEn: To make something impure or unsafe by introducing harmful substances.
example: Leaking chemicals from the mine contaminated the groundwater near the village.

definitionEn: To reduce the amount of something until very little remains.
example: Overfishing has depleted fish stocks in the bay over the past decade.

definitionEn: To replace or restore something so that it lasts or continues.
example: Farmers renew the soil each season by adding compost and natural fertiliser.

definitionEn: To keep something going over a long period without running out.
example: Can the planet sustain our energy demands without damaging the environment?

definitionEn: To use up energy, fuel, or resources.
example: Older refrigerators consume far more electricity than modern models do.

definitionEn: To balance or cancel out an effect, such as carbon emissions, by making a compensating reduction elsewhere.
example: The airline offsets its emissions by funding tree planting projects in rural areas.

definitionEn: A factory where crude oil or sugar is processed into usable products.
example: The new refinery will turn crude oil into petrol and diesel for the region.

definitionEn: A structure in which a nuclear chain reaction is controlled to produce energy.
example: Engineers inspected the reactor for leaks before restarting the power plant.

definitionEn: To use something carefully so that it is not wasted or used up.
example: Turning off unused lights helps us conserve power and money at home.

definitionEn: To reduce or remove carbon dioxide emissions from an economy, industry, or energy system.
example: The government aims to decarbonise the electricity sector by the end of the decade.

definitionEn: The process by which green plants use sunlight to make food from water and carbon dioxide.
example: Photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy stored in plant tissue.

definitionEn: The process of burning a substance so that it releases heat and energy.
example: Incomplete combustion in older engines releases harmful carbon monoxide gas.

definitionEn: A chemical compound made only of hydrogen and carbon, found in fossil fuels.
example: Natural gas is a hydrocarbon that burns more cleanly than coal.

definitionEn: A chemical product derived from petroleum or natural gas.
example: Many plastics are made from petrochemical feedstocks refined at large plants.

definitionEn: The simultaneous production of electricity and useful heat from a single fuel source.
example: Cogeneration allows the factory to reuse waste heat for its own processes.

definitionEn: Relating to or caused by motion, especially the energy an object has while moving.
example: Water turning a turbine converts kinetic energy into electrical power.

definitionEn: Relating to the combined electric and magnetic effects of charged particles.
example: Electromagnetic induction is the principle that makes most generators work.

definitionEn: A particle of light that carries electromagnetic energy.
example: Each photon carries a fixed amount of energy, depending on its frequency.

definitionEn: A measure of disorder in a system, which tends to increase over time.
example: Energy conversions always increase entropy, so some energy is lost as heat.

definitionEn: Describing power sources that can be switched on or off as needed to meet demand.
example: Gas-fired plants are dispatchable, so operators can ramp them up quickly.

definitionEn: The ability of a policy, technology, or treatment to produce the desired effect.
example: Researchers tested the efficacy of the new storage technology in harsh conditions.

definitionEn: The action of reducing the severity or harmful effects of something.
example: Climate mitigation requires cutting emissions across every major economic sector.

definitionEn: The reduction or removal of something harmful, such as pollution.
example: Pollution abatement equipment reduced soot from the chimney by nearly ninety percent.

definitionEn: A cost or benefit of an economic activity that affects others who did not choose it.
example: Pollution from the factory is an externality that the town had to bear.

definitionEn: Money given by a government to reduce the cost of a product or service.
example: The government offered a generous subsidy to households installing efficient heaters.

definitionEn: The reduction of output, supply, or use, often to limit excess generation or waste.
example: Wind farms face curtailment when the grid cannot absorb all their power.

definitionEn: The basic physical systems of a country, such as roads, power, and water.
example: Investment in grid infrastructure is essential for connecting new energy sources.

definitionEn: The ability of a system or technology to grow or be expanded to meet larger demand.
example: Engineers questioned the scalability of the prototype for national use.

definitionEn: The quality of being irregular or occurring at uneven intervals, as with some energy sources.
example: Intermittency of sunlight and wind makes stable power supply difficult to guarantee.

definitionEn: The minimum level of electricity demand that a power system must supply continuously.
example: Nuclear plants provide reliable baseload power that runs day and night.

definitionEn: Relating to rules or controls set by an authority to govern an industry or activity.
example: The regulatory agency approved the new emissions standards after months of review.

definitionEn: The removal of government rules and controls from an industry, often to encourage competition.
example: Deregulation of the electricity market allowed new companies to enter the business.

definitionEn: The transfer of a publicly owned company or service into private ownership.
example: Privatisation of the national grid sparked a debate about prices and fairness.

definitionEn: The process of safely shutting down and dismantling a facility at the end of its life.
example: Decommissioning the old reactor will take more than fifteen years to complete.

meaningVi: lắp đặt bổ sung để cải tiến
definitionEn: To fit new equipment or parts to an existing building or machine to improve it.
example: The council will retrofit older schools with better insulation and efficient lighting.

definitionEn: The ability of a system to withstand shocks and recover quickly from disruption.
example: Diversifying supply improves the resilience of the power network during storms.

meaningVi: sự cô lập, lưu giữ carbon
definitionEn: The long-term capture and storage of carbon dioxide to keep it out of the atmosphere.
example: Carbon sequestration beneath the seabed could hold emissions for thousands of years.

definitionEn: The process of trapping carbon dioxide from the air or from industrial exhaust.
example: Direct air capture is expensive, but it could complement emission cuts.

definitionEn: The process of splitting a compound into its elements by passing electric current through it.
example: Electrolysis of water produces hydrogen and oxygen gas in a controlled reaction.

definitionEn: Irregular, chaotic movement of air or fluid that wastes energy in machines.
example: Turbulence in the airflow reduced the turbine's overall efficiency significantly.

definitionEn: The scientific study of the movement, distribution, and quality of water on Earth.
example: Hydrology experts modelled river flows to plan the location of the new dam.

definitionEn: A physical force produced by moving electric charges, which attracts or repels certain metals.
example: Magnetism between the rotor and stator generates the electricity in the turbine.

definitionEn: The ability of a material to allow electricity or heat to pass through it.
example: Copper has high conductivity, which is why it is used in most electrical wiring.

definitionEn: The quality of performing consistently well over time without failure.
example: Grid operators worry about the reliability of supply during long periods of calm weather.

definitionEn: A hard, shiny type of coal with a high carbon content and little smoke when burned.
example: Anthracite burns hot and clean, making it valuable for heating older homes.

definitionEn: A soft brown coal with low energy content, formed from partly decayed plant matter.
example: Lignite is cheap to mine but releases more carbon dioxide per unit of heat.

definitionEn: Describing a soft coal that contains bitumen and burns with a smoky flame.
example: Bituminous coal is the most common type used to generate power in many countries.

definitionEn: A thick, flammable liquid found underground, refined into fuels and chemicals.
example: Petroleum prices rose sharply after the pipeline was damaged in the storm.

definitionEn: A soft sedimentary rock that can contain oil or gas trapped in its layers.
example: Engineers extracted gas from shale formations using high-pressure fluid injection.

definitionEn: A technique of drilling deep underground and injecting fluid to crack rock and release gas.
example: Fracking has transformed the energy market but also raised environmental concerns.

definitionEn: The breakdown of organic material by heating it in the absence of oxygen.
example: Pyrolysis of waste plastic can produce oil that is used as a fuel.

definitionEn: The process of converting solid fuel, such as coal or biomass, into a combustible gas.
example: Gasification of coal produces syngas that can power turbines or make chemicals.

definitionEn: A mild heat treatment that dries and darkens biomass to make it more energy dense.
example: Torrefaction turns wood chips into a brittle fuel that is easier to transport.

definitionEn: Taking place in the absence of oxygen, as in certain forms of fermentation.
example: Anaerobic digestion of food waste produces methane that can be captured for power.

definitionEn: Requiring or taking place in the presence of oxygen.
example: Aerobic bacteria consume the organic matter quickly when enough oxygen is available.

definitionEn: Relating to the direct conversion of temperature differences into electric voltage.
example: Thermoelectric generators can power sensors using the heat from exhaust pipes.

definitionEn: Describing materials that generate an electric charge when they are squeezed or stressed.
example: Piezoelectric tiles under a busy footpath can capture energy from footsteps.

definitionEn: A material that conducts electricity with almost no resistance when cooled below a critical temperature.
example: Superconductor cables could carry large amounts of power over long distances.

definitionEn: The state in which a material carries electric current with zero resistance.
example: Superconductivity was discovered over a century ago but remains hard to apply widely.

definitionEn: Describing a material that can be strongly magnetised, like iron or nickel.
example: The generator's rotor is built from ferromagnetic steel to enhance its magnetic field.

definitionEn: The lag between a change in magnetic force and the resulting change in magnetisation.
example: Hysteresis losses in the transformer core waste part of the energy as heat.

definitionEn: The opposition that a circuit offers to alternating current, caused by inductance or capacitance.
example: High reactance in the cable reduces the power that reaches the distant substation.

definitionEn: The total opposition to alternating current in a circuit, combining resistance and reactance.
example: Matching the impedance of the inverter to the grid minimises energy losses.

definitionEn: The ability of a component to store electric charge, measured in farads.
example: Higher capacitance allows the circuit to store more charge for smoother output.

definitionEn: The property of a circuit that opposes changes in the current flowing through it.
example: The coil's inductance smooths out sudden spikes in the electric current.

definitionEn: A device that converts alternating current into direct current.
example: A rectifier at the charging station turns grid power into direct current for batteries.

definitionEn: A device that converts direct current into alternating current for household supply.
example: The solar inverter feeds the power from the roof into the household supply.

definitionEn: A device that changes the voltage of alternating current by electromagnetic induction.
example: The transformer steps up the voltage so that power travels efficiently across the country.

definitionEn: A heavy rotating wheel that stores kinetic energy and smooths out variations in motion.
example: The engineers installed a flywheel to store energy for brief power interruptions.

definitionEn: A capacitor that stores much more energy than ordinary capacitors and charges very quickly.
example: A supercapacitor can deliver a burst of power to start the motor in seconds.

definitionEn: A liquid or gel that conducts electricity through the movement of ions, used in batteries.
example: The electrolyte in the battery must stay stable across a wide range of temperatures.

definitionEn: An electrode where reduction occurs, typically the positive terminal of a battery during discharge.
example: Lithium ions move from the anode to the cathode when the battery discharges.

definitionEn: An electrode where oxidation occurs, typically the negative terminal of a battery during discharge.
example: Graphite is widely used as the anode in modern lithium-ion batteries.

definitionEn: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up in the process.
example: A platinum catalyst helps convert hydrogen and oxygen into water in fuel cells.

definitionEn: Relating to entropy, the measure of disorder or unavailable energy in a system.
example: Every entropic process leaves less useful energy than before for future work.

definitionEn: The branch of physics dealing with heat, work, and the energy relationships in physical systems.
example: Thermodynamics explains why no engine can convert all its heat into useful work.

definitionEn: A measure of the total heat content of a system at constant pressure.
example: The enthalpy of combustion for natural gas determines how much heat it releases.

definitionEn: The maximum useful work that can be extracted from a system as it reaches equilibrium with its surroundings.
example: Analysing exergy shows where the plant loses the most useful energy.

definitionEn: Relating to heat energy, especially the amount of heat a fuel produces when burned.
example: The calorific value of wood varies with its moisture content and species.

definitionEn: The calculation of the quantities of reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
example: Stoichiometry tells engineers how much oxygen a fuel needs for complete combustion.

definitionEn: A form of the same chemical element with a different number of neutrons in its nucleus.
example: Uranium isotope enrichment is central to the operation of many nuclear reactors.

definitionEn: The spontaneous emission of radiation from the unstable nuclei of certain atoms.
example: Radioactivity decreases over time as unstable atoms gradually decay into stable forms.

definitionEn: The time taken for half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay.
example: The half-life of this isotope is about thirty years, so it stays hazardous for long.

definitionEn: Capable of undergoing nuclear fission when struck by neutrons.
example: Uranium-235 is fissile, so it sustains the chain reaction inside the reactor core.

definitionEn: The joining of light atomic nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing huge amounts of energy.
example: Nuclear fusion powers the sun, combining hydrogen nuclei into helium.

definitionEn: Relating to a material that obeys Ohm's law, with current directly proportional to voltage.
example: Ohmic resistors keep the relationship between voltage and current linear.

definitionEn: The standard unit of energy, equal to the work done by one newton moving one metre.
example: One kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 million joules, a useful figure for energy bills.
